thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] inference-api: elevated 502s and stream disconnects  region=us-west-2a  error_rate=12% (>alert)  playbook=inference-az-network-degrade

lina_oncall: picking this up. dashboards show NLB target flips and "unhealthy" counts only for nodes in us-west-2a. streaming sessions drop after ~10-30s. tagging @mike_neteng for deeper network triage.

mike_neteng: looking. VPC flow logs + host metrics point to two things: 1) repeated ARP unresolved events on a subset of hosts, 2) nf_conntrack nearing max on g5 fleet (conntrack_count ~ 98% of limit), causing new TCP sessions to be dropped. also seeing ENA driver tx-queue stalls on 8 hosts in us-west-2a.

lina_oncall: customer impact: "multiple customers on Dedicated pools in us-west-2a experience websocket reconnect churn and 502s on short-lived requests". marking P1 and notifying CS.

tara_support: Customer X reported streaming broken; they rely on pinned AZ capacity. Can we provide ETA for failover or migration?

lina_oncall: Immediate actions: 1) reduce new allocations to us-west-2a (scheduler flag), 2) enable connection draining on NLB targets and reduce healthcheck sensitivity, 3) bump conntrack max on canary hosts, 4) open AWS ticket. Executing 1-3 now.

devops-bot: schedctl: set-az-avoid us-west-2a duration=4h by lina_oncall  success

mike_neteng: applying conntrack bump on 4 canary nodes: 
```
echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
```

mike_neteng: also lowered NLB healthcheck threshold from 3->5 consecutive successes (to reduce flapping), enabled connection draining timeout=300s. doing this carefully to avoid prolonging failovers for stuck nodes.

lina_oncall: rolling-steer traffic away from us-west-2a via route weights: set us-west-2b=60%, us-west-2c=30%, us-west-2a=10%. starting gradual shift.

incident-bot: RouteManager: traffic weights updated by lina_oncall  change-id=7b9d  monitoring 60s

mike_neteng: starting tcpdump on one affected host; seeing bursts of ARP requests/failed retries then a flood of SYNs with no ACKs. conntrack table shows large number of TIME_WAIT and SYN_RECV entries. suspect kernel conntrack exhaustion + ENA queue bounce. attaching redacted sample.

aws-support: (via ticket) We see host-level ENA driver hang reports in us-west-2a) and are escalating to network/hypervisor team. Suggested mitigation: avoid allocating in AZ and migrate active pinned workloads.

lina_oncall: spinning up replacement capacity in us-west-2b (8 nodes) and us-west-2c (5 nodes), priming model loads and KV cache. starting migrations for customers who accept.

tara_support: Customer Y accepted migration to us-west-2b; moving now. Customer Z requests wait-for-postmortem before migrating.

mike_neteng: created an iptables conntrack helper shim for canaries to reject new SYNs when conntrack > threshold to protect control plane, example: 
```
# pseudo
if [ $(cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count) -gt 240000 ]; then
  iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -j REJECT
fi
```

lina_oncall: that's defensive but risky. limit to canary subset and monitor.

incident-bot: ASGManager: new instances launching in us-west-2b/us-west-2c  launched=13  warming

mike_neteng: AWS responded again: their telemetry shows ENI TX queue stalls caused by a hypervisor-side scheduling regression under heavy ARP/NAT churn. they recommend avoiding the AZ until they remediate.

lina_oncall: we've set scheduler avoidance and are stopping new infra builds in us-west-2a. routing weights decreased traffic and overall 502s dropped from 12% -> 2.5% across the region. still seeing occasional reconnects for pinned sessions.

tara_support: notified all impacted customers: short note: "We've isolated an AZ-local network plane issue in us-west-2a; we've steered traffic and offered migrations. We'll follow up with a postmortem."

mike_neteng: short-term host fix: rolling reboot of affected hosts to clear ENA driver state and conntrack leaks. starting batch 1 now (3 hosts). will monitor conntrack counts post-reboot.

lina_oncall: handoff plan: I'll hand to @mike_neteng for 03:30Z extended mitigation. leaving notes: avoidance enabled, conntrack bumps applied on canaries, NLB healthcheck tuned, migrations in progress, AWS ticket open (CASE-987654321).

mike_neteng: taking over. next steps: 1) coordinate with AWS for capture and logs, 2) run scheduled reboots in controlled batches, 3) export conntrack metric history for postmortem, 4) implement automated scheduler-avoid trigger on conntrack/excess-nlb-unhealthy metrics.

incident-bot: CloudWatch: nf_conntrack_count > 80% correlated with NLB UnhealthyHostCount spikes between 03:05-03:18Z

aws-support: update: Our infra team confirmed a hypervisor scheduling regression causing ENA driver TX queuing to back up under high ARP/NAT churn; fix is being rolled to impacted hosts. Estimated AZ-wide remediation 70-100 minutes.

mike_neteng: completed first reboot batch  hosts=3  all passed healthchecks and conntrack counts fell to <40% on those nodes. 502s for migrated customers are resolved.

tara_support: Customer X reports restored streams after migration; Customer Z still pinned and experiencing occasional reconnects, will follow up about migration window.

mike_neteng: action items captured: - keep scheduler avoidance on us-west-2a for 4h - continue controlled reboots while watching conntrack and ENA stats - automate fallback routing when unhealthy-hosts > threshold - collect packet captures and conntrack dumps for postmortem - coordinate CS comms

lina_oncall: closing handoff. thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (monitoring). region us-west-2a flagged as "limited" for new allocations.

mike_neteng: final note: root cause likely interplay of ENA/hypervisor scheduling regression + conntrack exhaustion driven by ARP/NAT churn. postmortem will include timeline, customer impact list, and infra changes (scheduler-avoid auto-trigger, conntrack threshold alarms, and ASG warmup improvements).

tara_support: dropping final customer note and prepping PM for postmortem. :mailbox_with_mail:

incident-bot: closing thread log.
